title.narrative: Public Financial Management Technical Assistance Project

description.narrative: Achieving effective and transparent management of public finances as an enabler of poverty reducing programs and economic growth

The Public Financial Management Project for Moldova aims to achieve effective and transparent management of public finances - as an enabler o f poverty-reducing programs and economic growth. The project consists of the following components: Component 1) will finance US$ 1 1.199 million worth of international and local consulting services, training, information systems, and office-related equipment, in three subcomponents: Budget Formulation Methodology; Budget Execution Methodology; and Financial Management Information System (FMIS). Component 2) will finance US$ 1.237 million worth of international and local consulting services, training, information technology and office-related equipment, in three subcomponents: Normative and Legal Framework for Internal Control and Audit; Transformation o f Financial Control into Internal Audit Function; and Expanding the Internal Audit to Line Ministries and Sub-national Entities. Component 3) will develop a sustainable institutional training capacity to develop civil servants' skills in key areas of public financial management. Component 4) will finance US$ 0.878 million worth of international and local consulting services, training, some limited information technology and running costs. Financing for this component will be provided by the Dutch Government through a trust fund.

title.narrative: Public financial decisions in the government entities follow sound PEM rules and procedures and are based on reliable financial data

target.value: Useful and timely data generated by FMIS system. Budget classification and chart of accounts aligned with GFS 2001. Decision-makershave access to reliable financial data.

actual.value: The new BPS module supports the new budget classification / chart of accounts (compatible with international standards), as well asmedium term budget framework (MTBF) and key performance indicators for central and local government budgets

title.narrative: Overall fiscal discipline and strategic resource allocation improved (as evidenced by the IMF monitoring assessment)

baseline.value: The actual fiscal surplus during 2003-05 is better than in the approved budgets. The expenditure arrears in 2005 at 3% of totalexpenditure. Budget has little correlation with EGPRSP priorities.

target.value: Fiscal deficit is less than 2% of GDP by the end of 2011, and less than 1% of GDP by end 2012. No new arreas accumulated, existingarrears fully cleared. Medium-term and annual sectoral allocation tend to match government policy priori

comment.narrative: The indicator will be monitored further based on the parameters of the current Government program agreed with IMF

actual.value: As of end of September 2013, the fiscal deficit was 0.6 billion MDL or around 0.9% of projected GDP for the period.

title.narrative: The Academy of Public Administration has capacity to train civil servants in conducting training in 18 new training modules.

baseline.value: The Academy has established a Department of Civil Service Training. The first training in management and internal control systems is being prepared, local trainers are trained for this module.

target.value: The Academy delivers training to civil servants in 18 training modules related to organizational and financial management. Trainerstrained.

actual.value: A training strategy will be scaled down to BPS and basic ICT support needs. The revision of this strategy is expected to be completed in early 2014. In the meantime, 12 MoF officials have been trained as “trainers” to assist in the training of budget users. The supplier is expected to complete the training on all modules delivered under the reduced scope in December 2013
